sections.Usage:
Usage of the Adjustable Chain Gearshift

To control the speed of an encased chain, the Adjustable Chain Gearshift must be placed in line with
Encased Chain Drives
with sides touching. 
To increase the speed of an encased chain, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift must be connected to the source of rotational power by its axis and it must be powered by a redstone signal. A full strength redstone signal will double the speed of the chain.  A partial strength signal, such as given by an analog lever, will give a proportional increase in speed between 1x and 2x.

If a redstone-powered Adjustable Chain Gearshift receives its rotational power from an encased chain, then it will reduce the rotation speed of its axis by up to half, again depending on the strength of the redstone signal.

Using an analog lever, the following gear ratios can be obtained:
sections.Examples:
Other means to apply RPM ratios only make it possible to double or halve the speed (using
cogwheels
,
Sequenced Gearshifts
...). Using combinations of the speed ratios above, it is theoretically possible to approach any RPM ratio, and therefore any RPM.

For example, when trying to build a real time clock,
Clockwork Bearings
can't be used (they display in-game time instead). A
Mechanical Bearing
spinning at 1 RPM works for the second hand, because it has to perform 1 full cycle of the clock per minute. However, the minute hand should be 60 times slower, running at 1/60 RPM, and the hour hand 12 times slower than the minute hand. To reach ratios of 60:1 and 12:1, which are not powers of 2, an Adjustable Chain Gearshift is required. A working combination in that case is:

Decrease speed at a ratio of 15:8 with power 13, and halve the speed 5 times (32:1). The result is a ratio of 480:8 = 60:1.
Decrease speed at a ratio of 3:2 with power 7, and halve the speed 3 times (8:1). The result is a ratio of 24:2 = 12:1.

In a niche use case, you need to perform a rotation of 1 radian. To get an accurate angle, a
Valve Handle
can be used, but they only work in degrees. There are exactly π radians in 180 degrees, so applying a ratio of approximately π:1 to a Valve Handle set to 180 degrees would work. This process can get quite tedious, especially for situations like this with no obvious solution, that require chained Adjustable Chain Gearshifts. In that case, the
RPM Ratio Finder
is an online tool that can help find a working combination. Below is an example for a π:1 ratio.

A valid combination approaching a π:1 ratio, provided by the RPM Ratio Finder. The numbers are the redstone power to feed the Adjustable Chain Gearshifts.

sections.Usage:
Much like a
Chest
, an Adjustable Crate placed next to another crate will form a larger crate equivalent in storage to two individual crates.
sections.Container:
An adjustable crate has 16 slots of inventory space, and two combined crates have 32 slots of inventory space.

Crates open when used and, unlike chests, can be opened when there is an opaque block above them.

The storage space of a crate can be adjusted by scrolling with the cursor over the second number of the crate's GUI. Holding shift while scrolling will adjust by one slot (64 items) at a time.

When an adjustable crate is filled with items that do not stack to 64, the number of items in the crate can show as being less than the maximum, while still not allowing more items to be placed inside.

sections.Intro: Learn to design and build your own large-scale ore processing facility. This tutorial covers the concepts and peculiarities of each step of the process. Along the way, you'll learn how to sort, buffer, and regulate the item flow between steps so your processing line stays efficient, unclogged, and fully automated.

sections.Big Picture:
Flowchart for Automated Ore Processing

Large-scale ore processing begins with large-scale ore collection, which means using a mining contraption. Ore and other items collected by the mining contraption must then be transferred to the ore processing facility. Ore is then crushed and washed to produce nuggets. The nuggets are packed into ingots and blocks then sent to storage facilities. Each of these
processing steps
will be discussed in detail.

Mining contraptions pick up a lot of things besides ore, so items must be buffered and filtered before each step. Those items which should not go through a particular step must be sent along a bypass. These and other
flow control
concepts will be discussed in a later section.

sections.Processing Steps:
Though there are a great many possible designs for a complete ore processing system, an example is displayed below which will be referenced in the discussion of the processing steps and flow control.

Full Ore Processor with Annotated Processing Steps
sections.Collecting:
Collecting of ore and other blocks will almost always be done with a mechanical mining contraption. See
Tutorials/Mining Contraptions
for a full description. The type and size of mining contraption must be considered in the layout of the ore processor.
sections.Transferring:
A
Portable Storage Interface
(PSI) will transfer all the items from the mining contraption to the initial
storage buffer
. The PSI devices on the mining contraption and ore processor must have exactly one or two spaces between them. Note that placing the mining contraption will not initiate a connection between the two PSIs. Instead, place two minecart tracks on the ground. Then place the contraption on the first track block and roll it into position for the transfer.

As depicted by the chest in the annotated image above, it is always a good idea to also have a way to manually transfer items.
sections.Crushing:
Items which cannot be crushed will be destroyed if dropped into crushing wheels. Therefore, items in the initial storage buffer must be
filtered
to bypass the crushing wheels for non-crushable items. See the figure
Example of Collection Buffering and Crush Bypass
below for an example of how to construct a bypass.

The time needed to crush a stack of items can range from a few seconds to a couple minutes.  The
crushing speed
depends on the type of item, the stack size, and the rotations per minute (RPM). Large stack sizes and high RPM will increase the crushing speed. For example, crushing multiple stacks of 16 cobblestone at an RPM of 16 will provide an output of 26 items per minute. Increasing the stack size to 64 increases the output rate to 83 items per minute. Increasing the RPM from 16 to 64 increases the 83 items per minute to 295.

When feeding the crushing wheels, be sure to use brass funnels or smart chutes and set their maximum output to up to 64. Normal chutes will output a maximum stack size of 16, and andesite funnels put out items one at a time.

The final way to increase crushing throughput is to use multiple pairs of crushing wheels. Just be sure to feed the items evenly amongst the wheels and to build your power source to handle the heavy stress of multiple wheels.
sections.Washing:
Washing is normally done with multiple fans set side-by-side blowing across water and one or more mechanical belts holding the items to be washed. A stack of 1 - 16 items needs to have damp air blown across it for 7.5 seconds to fully wash. Stacks of 17-32 items need 15 seconds and 49-64 need 30 seconds. The more fans you have, the faster the belt speed can be and still keep your items in the damp air for the required time. A chart at
Encased_Fan#Bulk Item Processing Speed
provides various options for number of fans and belt speed.

Note that the speed of the fan has no impact on the time needed to wash a stack. Rather, the speed controls how many blocks (or in this case, belts) will be covered with the damp air. A little experimentation shows that 1 RPM will extend the wash 3 blocks which will just cover the first belt. Eight RPM covers 2 belts; 24 RPM - 3 belts, 32 RPM - 4 belts.

Wash Bypass

To increase throughput of washing, increase the belt speed and number of fans in tandem or add more belts in parallel. Note that you can sometimes increase the belt speed a little more than the chart states because as the washed items transform, some of them create two new items. Washing gravel, for instance, will often give you a stack of flint and a stack of iron nuggets. When this happens, the flint on the belt pauses as the iron nugget moves forward. This means any gravel behind the flint on the belt will also pause for a bit giving it a little extra time in the wash.

As with crushing, it is wise to route items you don't want to wash through a bypass. It doesn't normally hurt unwashable items to go through the wash, but doing so will decrease the washing throughput. The figure labeled
Wash Bypass
shows a simple configuration. The crushing wheels drop items into the double chest. Brass funnels on the face of the chest filter for items you wish to wash and place them on the washing belts. On the end of the double chest, another brass funnel has the same
List Filter
but now set to "deny." This funnel empties onto another belt that bypasses the wash phase.
sections.Packing:
The packing step uses a mechanical press and basin to combine small items into their bulk forms. For example, nine iron nuggets will pack into one iron ingot. Nine iron ingots will pack into one iron block. The packing step generates no waste items so just before the packing step is a good time to weed out items you don't want to keep. See the section on
Discarding
below for more information.

Brass Tunnel Sorter

Introducing non-packable items to the packing basin will quickly and permanently clog the system. So, it is critical to separate the packable from the non-packable items. The figure
Brass Tunnel Sorter
to the right shows a simple way to filter on a moving belt rather than from a storage buffer as described earlier. In this design, non-packable items continue straight through the tunnel and on to the storage system. Packable items are diverted to a side belt that deposits the items in the storage buffer prior to packing.

Packing is a simple process in theory—put nine of the same items in a basin and press them into a single item. The process becomes very complicated, however, when there are several different types of items that need packing and they come in random order and intervals. Basins have nine inventory slots in them, each of which can accumulate up to a full stack of any particular item. When enough items have accumulated to match one of the packing recipes, items are removed from the inventory. No two inventory slots can hold the same type of item though.

Packing Design

Clogging
can happen if all nine inventory slots in a basin have items in them and the next item in queue is a tenth type of item. That item will be held back until one of the inventory slots empties. But if there are not enough of a particular item type to complete a recipe, then the inventory stack will never deplete. The system is permanently clogged until you clean it out manually. See
Basin#Clogging
for more detail.

Packing is also a very slow process. To prevent clogging, you need a good size storage buffer, and you need to limit each basin to no more than nine types of items. If you have more than nine packable item types, then you will need more basins, each tuned to their own set of allowed item types. The figure
Packing Design
to the right shows an example of how this is done. Items to be packed enter from the diagonal belt on the right into an item vault acting as a storage buffer. Two smart chutes convey items from the storage buffer through a hopper to a basin. Each smart chute is filtered for a different set of item types to ensure than no more than nine item types are fed to either basin. The basin outputs are also filtered to ensure only the proper packing recipes are completed.

Metal nuggets require two packing steps, the first to pack nuggets into ingots, and the second to pack ingots into blocks. This can easily be done by putting two basins and mechanical presses in sequence. This design, however, uses a loop-back approach which is more compact, if perhaps a bit slower. The basins output their items to the belt at a place before the tunnel that sorts out packable items. That way ingots created by packing will be routed back to the same basin to be packed into metal blocks.
sections.Storing:
Storage

The only feasible way of storing the large volumes of items output by the ore processor is with large item vaults. You may very well need to connect multiple item vaults into a
Logistics Network
to handle even larger volumes of output. The output of the ore processor is fed by belt through a brass funnel into the item vault. To monitor the contents of the item vault and extract specific items you will need to attach a
Packager
,
Stock Link
, and a
Stock Ticker
or
Redstone Requester
. See
Packager
for details.

Item vaults should also have an
Item Hatch
attached for each manual deposits.
sections.Buffering:
Each processing step proceeds at its own rate, sometimes varying between different types of items within the same processing step. It is very important, then, to buffer the items in some form of storage block before each step.

For example, a bulk transfer of items from a mining contraption will happen much faster than crushing wheels can process. So, transfer the items into an item vault first where they can rapidly accumulate. The item vault will then send the items out at whatever rate the crushing wheels can accept. Similarly, crushing is typically faster than washing, so you will need to buffer the crushing output too.
sections.Filtering and Bypassing:
Example of Collection Buffering and Crush Bypass

Mining contraptions pick up a lot of things besides ore: diamonds, lapus lazuli, amethyst, wood, etc. Metal ores need to go through each of the processing steps: crushing, washing, packing. Some things, such as wood, should bypass all of the processing steps.  Things like plants, amethyst clusters, and blaze rods, you may want to crush but not wash. Diamonds and lapis lazuli should not be crushed or washed, but you may still want to pack them into blocks. Gravel presents a rare case where you may want to skip crushing but still wash it to create iron nuggets.

Fortunately, the storage blocks used in buffering provide a great point to sort the items and bypass specific steps.  For example (see image to right), smart chutes can gravity feed specific listed items from the bottom of an item vault into crushing wheels, while another smart chute off to the side bypasses the crushing wheels for all of the other items. Brass funnels can likewise feed specific items onto the washing belt while diverting everything else to a bypass belt.

Since multiple types of items must be filtered, you will have to use an
Item Filter
. For each smart chute or brass funnel, construct an item filter with the things you want to pass through the upcoming processing step. In most cases all of the item filters will have identical lists of items. (They may differ sometimes to prevent clogging.) For the bypass route, use the same list of items but set the filter to "deny-list" so that everything
except
those items will pass. It is important that the pass and bypass filters have the same item list to prevent unforeseen items from clogging the storage buffer.

A buffer is not needed going into the storage step because the storage operation happens very fast. Filtering items before storage will often be done on belts with a
Brass Tunnel
. The same duplicate item list concept applies. One output of the tunnel should have the item filter set to "allow-list" and the other output should have it set to "deny-list."

Selectively discarding unwanted items
sections.Discarding: There are some items you may wish to simply discard such as flint and deepslate. There are several ways to selectively discard items. One method is shown in the image to the right. Simply place a filtered smart chute under a mechanical belt where all of the items will pass. Those items matching the filter will drop off the belt and be discarded below the smart chute. Fill in the surrounding area with grass blocks to keep the trash out of site and to prevent accidently picking it up.
sections.Clog Prevention:
Clogging is a temporary or permanent stoppage of item processing in all or part of the ore processor. Temporary stoppages can occur when the buffer storage between two processing steps becomes full and cannot accept any more input. This causes the step before the buffer storage to completely stop until some storage room frees up.  If the deposit of new ore into the processor happens at sufficiently spaced intervals, then a larger buffer size may solve the problem as the downstream processing will continue between ore deposits. A more reliable approach is to increase the speed of the downstream processing. A good example of this would be increasing the speed and length of the washing belts which increases their throughput.  Alternatively, you could put more washing belts in parallel. But for this, you will have to devise a buffering method that insures all the belts get fed evenly.

Another type of clogging occurs when a basin is fed with more than nine types of items. If the basin is used with a mechanical press to pack items, this will cause the packing process to stop completely. To prevent this, filter the input of the basin so that no more than nine types of items can enter.  If there are more than nine item types to be packed, you will have to add another basin and mechanical press filtered to accept the additional items. See
Basin#Clogging
for a full discussion.

sections.Usage: While held, funnels prevent the player from accessing inventories, instead placing them.
sections.Placement:
Sneak
right clicking with a Funnel places it in input mode.

Right-clicking a funnel on a
Mechanical Belt

When attached to a
Contraption
, Andesite Funnels can drop items from the contraption's inventory or pick up items that collide with it.
sections.Input/Output:
When outputting to dropped items, the Funnel waits until the previous dropped item is removed before dropping another stack.

The Andesite Funnel outputs only one item at a time, but can input entire stacks.

When not on a
Mechanical Belt
, a
Wrench
can be
used
to set it to extract or insert. Otherwise, the direction of the belt determines whether the Funnel extracts or inserts.

Redstone
can be applied to stop the funnel from inputting or outputting.

sections.Catches fire from lava:
The
Basin
is a block that holds items and fluids used in
Packing
,
Compacting
, and
Mixing
recipes. A basin can also function as an interaction point in fluid systems as fluids can be placed in or removed from a Basin directly by a player. In a survival game, a basin's most significant function is creating
Brass
, which is essential for the creation of most advanced components.

sections.Packing, Compacting, and Mixing:
Basins can be used in conjunction with a
Mechanical Mixer
to apply Mixing recipes and with a
Mechanical Press
to apply Packing and Compacting recipes. If a Basin is placed two blocks below a powered Mechanical Mixer or Mechanical Press, the mixer or press will activate as soon as the basin contains all the ingredients for a valid recipe.

Some mixing recipes (including that of brass) require a heated or super-heated
Blaze Burner
to be directly underneath the basin. A basin's filter slot can be used to restrict which recipes will be performed. Right-click the filter slot with the desired item to set the filter.
sections.Inventory: A basin can contain both items and fluids. A basin has 9 inventory slots, each of which can hold up to one stack of items or up to 1000 mB of each fluid. Each inventory slot must hold a different type of item or fluid, so room is kept for other recipe items rather than allowing all slots to be filled with the same item.
sections.Input Output:
Items can be added by hoppers, funnels, and
Chutes
. Fluids can be added by
Fluid Pipes
and by
Deployers
holding buckets and bottles. Basins can also take in items floating in the world in and directly above their block space. Players can interact with a basin's fluid inventory in a similar manner to vanilla cauldrons.

A basin can output its item products to another basin, a
Mechanical Belt
, a
Depot
, a
Chute
, a pair of
Crushing Wheels
, or an
Item Drain
. A basin can output fluid products to another basin or an
Item Drain
. Additionally, A basin will drop all of its items when flipped upside down in a
contraption
.

The destination of the output must be in the block directly below an air block directly next to the basin.
If a basin has a valid output destination, a spout will appear on the side of the basin, "pouring" the items out of the basin and to the destination. If multiple output destinations are possible, right clicking the basin with a Wrench will change the location of the spout.
sections.Fluid Logistics:
Since fluids in basins can be added and removed directly by players, Basins provide a valuable interaction point with fluid logistics systems. For instance, it can allow players to manually fill or empty a
Fluid Tank
connected to a basin by a
Mechanical Pump
.

Outputting a potion of weakness from a mixer-basin

To extract a fluid from a pipe, such as a potion, without also extracting the inputted water use a smart fluid pipe. Create and apply a
filter
set to blacklist water (using a water bucket). Then use a mechanical pump to draw the fluid along into a second basin. From there you can send it to a spout if desired.
sections.Clogging:
Basins, whether used with a mechanical press or a mechanical mixer, can sometimes stop operating due to clogging. Clogging happens when three conditions coincide.

The basin's inventory slots hold nine different types of items
There are not enough of any type of item to complete a recipe
The input device attempts to insert a tenth type of item

When these conditions coincide, the new basin will neither accept the new item nor output any items.

There are two ways to unclog a basin. Either manually extract the basin inventory so it can begin refilling or change the item that the input device is trying to insert to a type that the basin already holds. To prevent clogging, filter the input so that no more than nine types of items can be inserted into any particular basin. This may require multiple basins with different input filtering to cover the desired span of recipes.

sections.In-Game Tooltip:
Detects items and entities passing by on a
Mechanical Belt
in front of it. Use a
Wrench
to cycle its behaviour. Non-items will always be handled in detect mode regardless of the setting.
Detect Mode
Provides redstone while a matching item is in the observed belt segment.
Pulse Mode
Emits a pulse when a matching item passes the center of the observed belt segment.
Eject Mode
Ejects matching items off the side. If the target belt or space is occupied, the item will be held in place.
Split Mode
Splits a matching item stack and ejects half of it off the side.

A
Blaze Burner
is a heating component that is required for certain
Mixing
recipes. It can be used for heating

,

sections.Filling an Empty Blaze Burner:
Blaze Burners must have Blazes in them to function. To put a Blaze in an Empty Blaze Burner, right-click on a
Blaze
while holding an Empty Blaze Burner. Alternatively, an Empty Blaze Burner can be filled by right-clicking on a Blaze Spawner. This method can be repeated without risk of destroying the Blaze Spawner.
sections.Heating:
Blaze Burners are used for Heating and Super-Heating
Basins
when doing
Mixing
recipes. In particular, they are required to make
Brass
. They can also be used as a heat source for boilers used to power
Steam Engines
. When a heat-able block is placed above a fueled Blaze Burner, the Burner will appear to channel heat into the block.

Right-clicking a Blaze Burner with any item that can be used as
Furnace
fuel will temporarily put it in a Heated state. Right-clicking a Blaze Burner with a
Blaze Cake
will temporarily put it in a Super-Heated state.

Fuel burn time is the same as a vanilla
Furnace
. The Blaze inside changes its size and texture depending on the amount of fuel provided, following the phases:

Phase 1 — Smouldering — Does not provide any heat for mixing, but provides the "passive" heat level for boilers (for more details see
Heat sources
). This is the default state when placing the Burner or when the fuel runs out.
Phase 2 — Heated/Kindled — Enables recipes that require heating. Lasts for the fuel's burn time and provides 1 heating level to
Steam Engines
per
Blaze Burner
Phase 3 — Super-Heated/Seething — Enables every
Mixing
recipe and provides 2 heating levels to
Steam Engines
per
Blaze Burner
. Only achievable using the
Blaze Cake
. Always lasts for 160 seconds. The Blaze Burner cannot be re-fed during this phase.

Notably, throwing an
Egg
at it will also generate heat. See the trivia section for more info.

A
Deployer
or
Mechanical Arm
can be used to automatically fuel the blaze burner by giving it a burnable item as input. If lava is used, the bucket will not be consumed. They will stop adding fuel if the Blaze Burner's remaining burn time is over 500 seconds, so no fuel is wasted. The exception to this is lava, which will be refueled at (and waste) 20 seconds, since lava completely fills the burner's maximum capacity of 1000 seconds.
sections.Train Controlling:
When assembled with a
Train
and given a
Train Schedule
, it will drive the
Train
to the
Train Stations
the schedule specifies.
sections.Stock Keeper:
You can also place a Blaze Burner beside a
Stock Ticker
for the burner to become a stock keeper. The Blaze Burner will display the heated phase without the heating function. As a little decoration, the Blaze inside the Blaze Burner gains a shopkeeper hat.
sections.Decoration:
Blaze Burners can be given a set of
Engineer's Goggles
by right-clicking them with goggles in hand. This does not consume the goggles, and is purely cosmetic.

Empty Blaze Burners can be lit on fire with a
Flint and Steel
as a decorative block. While lit, they can be given
Soul Sand
or
Soul Soil
to turn the fire into
Soul Fire
. These do not serve as heat for mixer recipes. However, they can be used as a passive heat source for
Steam Engine
boilers and for
Bulk Smoking
and
Bulk Haunting
using the
lit
and
soul fire
versions respectively.
sections.Trivia:
The Blaze Burner is a reference to
Calcifer
from
Howl's Moving Castle
. This is reflected in the overall design, the associated
advancement
being called "Sentient Fireplace", it burning blue when superheated and its ability to use eggs as fuel.

sections.Catches fire from lava:
The
Block of Copper
is a decorative storage block equivalent to nine
Copper Ingots
.
The block will oxidize, slowly becoming a blue-green color.

Cut Copper
,
Copper Shingles
, and
Copper Tiles
are purely decorative variants of the copper block and cannot be converted back into ingot form.

Blocks of copper can be mined only with a stone
pickaxe
or better. If a block of copper is mined without the use of a pickaxe, it drops nothing.

.

sections.Mod spotlights:
Mod spotlight by direwolf20 are YouTube videos introducing
Create
concepts and features. Note that the videos describe an earlier version of
Create
and many features have been updated:
Part 1
,
Part 2
,
Part 3
.
Part 4
sections.The Basics of Rotation:
A Rotating Encased belt block

Many machines and components in
Create
require
Rotational Force
to operate. Rotational force is generated by several
Kinetic Sources
such as the
Hand Crank
and the
Water Wheel
. Rotation can then be transmitted to Kinetic Appliances which perform a variety of actions with items such as a
Crushing Wheel
or a
Mechanical Saw
.

Rotational force has three characteristics: direction (clockwise, counter clockwise), speed in revolutions per minute (rpm), and
Kinetic Stress
(or power) measured in Stress Units (SU). Kinetic sources provide a specific number of stress units depending on the configuration of the source. Each kinetic appliance uses a certain number of stress units depending on the type of appliance and rotational speed. When the total number of stress units required by the attached appliances exceeds the number of stress units provided by the kinetic source, the kinetic source stops completely until the required stress units are reduced.
sections.Transmitting Rotational Force:
Transmitting power with shafts, belts, cogs and gearboxes.

Rotation can be transmitted in a straight line using a
Shaft
,
Mechanical Belt
, or
Encased Chain Drive
. The direction can be turned 90 degrees using a
Gearbox
or
Large Cogwheel
. The rotation can be temporarily stopped using a
Clutch
and can be reversed with a
Gearshift

The image to the right illustrates rotational power coming in from the top left via a length of connected shafts. The direction is turned 90 degrees downward using two large cogwheels. The vertical shaft then powers a gearbox that turns the direction of rotation to the right where a series of cogwheels, mechanical belts and gearboxes power a
Deployer
, a
Mechanical Press
, and a
Mechanical Mixer
.

These transmission components only transfer, stop, or convert rotational power. They do not consume any power [Unless changed in the
Config
] or change the speed of rotation.
sections.Changing Speed:
Just having components rotate is not always enough. Sometimes it is necessary to control the speed of rotation. This is especially important for machines that require a
minimum level of speed
to operate (e.g. the
Mechanical Mixer
). To make this possible, some kinetic blocks have the ability to
speed up
or
slow down
connected components:

Changing Speed with Cogwheels

Cogwheels
are not only useful for relaying rotation, but also serve as a simple way to control the speed. By attaching a large cogwheel diagonally to a regular sized one, one can double/half the speed of the other.

Powering the
large cogwheel
results in the
smaller
one turning at double the speed.

Powering the
small cogwheel
results in the
larger
one turning at half the speed.

Adjustable chain gearshift doubling the speed of an encased chain.

The
Adjustable Chain Gearshift
when used in combination with
Encased Chain Drive
s, gives finer control over speed than cogwheels. It can increase
input
speed for attached chain drives, or decrease
output
speed of shafts connected to chain drives.

While acting as an input, the adjustable chain gearshift will increase the speed of attached encased chain drives based on the analog redstone signal it receives. A full power redstone signal of 15 will double the speed of the chain drives while values below 15 will increase the speed proportionally between 1x and 2x. While acting as an output, it will reduce the speed of the chain drive in a similar manner. With no redstone signal, the speed will remain unchanged.
sections.Rotation Speed Controller:
While having a more expensive recipe, the
Rotation Speed Controller
also has the finest control over speed change. When a large cogwheel is attached to the controllers top, the large cogwheel, or shaft [depending on which one is powered] will spin at the configured speed in the
Values Settings Screen
.

).

sections.Materials:
Create adds many crafting ingredients for use throughout the mod. While some of them have few uses within Create itself at the moment, they are still handy connection points for pack-makers.

Andesite Alloy
, used for
Andesite Casing
and all the low-tier kinetic components.
Brass
, used in
Brass Casing
and more advanced kinetic blocks. Entry-point to the logistical components.
Copper
, generates in the world around surface level. Used for
Copper Casing
and fluid handling components, and used with Zinc to make Brass.
Zinc
, generates in the world. Used with Copper to make Brass.
sections.Other Materials:
Cinder Flour
, made from crushing
Netherrack
. Non renewable without 3rd party addons.
Polished Rose Quartz
, made from using
Sand Paper
on craft-able
Rose Quartz
. Used in the crafting of
Electron Tubes
and mixing of Chromatic Compound.
Powdered Obsidian
, made from crushing
Obsidian
. Used in several filling recipes and in the compacting of
Blaze Cake Bases
.
sections.Moving Contraptions:
Create allows you to move and animate block structures of any shape or form. This feature is extremely powerful as it proves useful in the field of automation, transportation and aesthetics.

In order to get the most out of this mechanic, it is helpful to know about the components and interactions involved in creating such structures.

Contraption Controllers
Contraption Assembly and Chassis Blocks
Portable Storage
Portable Actors
sections.Contraption Controllers:
Depending on the use case, different controllers can be used for mounting your structure. Some push, some pull, some rotate and some do it all at once.
These blocks have specific spaces where the anchor of the structure needs to be, and some can be configured to react differently to being stopped.
sections.Mechanical Piston:
Mechanical Pistons
are kinetically powered counterparts to Minecraft's
Pistons
. As such, they can push
super glued
blocks in front of them, and if sticky, pull them back.

However, Create's pistons do not work on their own. They require
Piston Extension Poles
added at the back, in order to be able to extend. When given
Rotational Force
, the piston will extend exactly as far as poles have been added to the back, rather than just 1 block space.
sections.Rope Pulley:
The
Rope Pulley
moves attached blocks and structures vertically. Use
Linear Chassis
,
Radial Chassis
or
Super Glue
to move more than a single block.

When powered by kinetics, it will start to move the attached structure. Speed and direction correlate to the incoming Rotation Speed.
sections.Mechanical Bearing:
The
Mechanical Bearing
is used for rotating larger structures with rotational force.

When Powered by kinetics, starts rotating the attached blocks.

Use Chassis or Super Glue to move more than a single block. Blocks that attach to other blocks, such as levers, torches,
Gantry Shafts
or
Mechanical Saws
will become part of the structure automatically.

Other attached
Mechanical Bearings
, if facing along the same axis as the original, will keep their alignment as the original rotates: See the GIFs for a visual example.
sections.Clockwork Bearing:
The
Clockwork Bearing
is an advanced version of the Mechanical Bearing for rotating up to two clock hands according to the current in-game time.

When powered by kinetics, starts rotating the attached structure towards the current hour. If an independent second structure exists in front of the first one, it will serve as the minute hand.
sections.Cart Assembler:
When placed on a Rail, the
Cart Assembler
can assemble and disassemble moving structures onto passing minecarts. Similarly to rotating structures, having a
Mechanical Bearing
in the structure will cause the attached part to keep the same alignment as the cart moves.

Single Cart contraptions as well as Carriage contraptions can carry items, liquids, or mobs, provided they have the correct storage blocks. They can also use Contrapion Actors such as the
Mechanical Saw
,
Drill
,
Harvester
,
Plough
or the
Portable Storage Interface
to interact with the world.

Carriage Contraptions are about the same, except their movement is smoother and thus it is easier to walk or ride on them without falling off. See
Trains
for further detail.

The
Ponder
scenes for the Funnel.

Funnels can be placed on inventories without the need to
sneak
, being placed in
output mode
by default.
Sneak

Funnels placed on a
Mechanical Belt
input or output depending on the belt's direction. A

When attached to a
Contraption
, Brass Funnels can drop items from the contraption's inventory or pick up items that collide with it. The filter is respected.
sections.Filtering:
Like other
Brass
machines, the Brass Funnel can be set to
Filter
items. It can also be set to output or input either "exactly" or "up to" a set amount of items via its
Value Settings Screen
. The maximum output stack size is 64.
sections.Input/Output:
When outputting to dropped items, the Funnel waits until the previous dropped item is removed before dropping another stack.

When not on a
Mechanical Belt
, a
Wrench
can be
used
to set it to extract or insert. Otherwise, the direction of the belt determines whether the Funnel extracts or inserts.

It can be turned off with
Redstone
.

Brass Tunnel
is a machine that can only be placed on

sections.Usage:
Brass Tunnels may be used on mechanical belts for four functions: 1) purely decorative, 2) splitting streams of items to multiple destinations, 3) sorting streams of items, and 4) combining multiple streams of items. Each tunnel can have an input or output portal on each of its four sides in a variety of combinations. The status of being an input or output depends purely on the direction of the belt touching a given side. A tunnel must straddle a belt, thus forcing at least one input and one output on opposite sides. The other two sides may have belts abutting the tunnel forming either input or output portals.

Tunnels which are placed immediately next to each other are automatically treated as a group, in most cases collecting from all inputs and distributing to all outputs. The way that items are distributed is controlled by the tunnels' value setting. Item stacks from different inputs will not be combined prior to distributing.
sections.Value Settings:
The
Value Settings Screen
can be accessed from the top of a tunnel. It is only viewable if the tunnel has more than two portals or is connected to other tunnels. All tunnels connected as a group will have the same value setting.
sections.Splitting Item Streams to Multiple Desti:
The
Split, Forced Split, Round Robin, Forced Round Robin, and Randomize
modes can be used to split one or more item input streams into multiple output streams. For example, a stream of logs may be split with half going to the fuel chamber of a furnace and half going to the smelting chamber. The
Forced Split
mode causes the output streams to have a nearly equal number of items while the
Forced Round Robin
causes the output streams to have nearly equal numbers of stacks. The
Split
and
Round Robin
will also keep the items or stacks evenly distributed as long as none of the outputs become obstructed. If that happens, the output will continue at the unobstructed ports. If single items rather than stacks enter a tunnel, the
Split
and
Forced Split
will default to
Round Robin
and
Forced Round Robin
behavior.
sections.Item Sorting:
Brass Tunnels can be
Filtered
to only allow certain items to pass. By placing different filters on the outputs of individual tunnels in a group, the cumulative input can be sorted. All items matching a filter will only pass through an output with that matching filter. They will not pass through an unfiltered output. Unfiltered outputs will pass all items that do not have a matching filter. If a particular filter is set on multiple tunnel outputs, then the distribution of the applicable items among the matching outputs will follow the value setting mode. Each group of outputs with common filters will apply the value setting mode independently.

Each individual tunnel within a group has its own space to hold an input item being sorted. Thus, in modes other than Synchronize Inputs, if all outputs through which a given type of item can be sent are blocked, tunnels that have received another item of that type block their inputs and cannot accept more items, but tunnels that have not received another item of that type (for example, tunnels that only receive a different item type) continue to accept input and deliver it to the proper (unblocked) outputs.
sections.Combining Multiple Item Streams:
Brass Tunnels can be used to combine items from different input streams forming a mixed output to one or more output portals. If there is only one output portal, then any value setting mode will work. If there are multiple outputs, then
Prefer Nearest
and
Synchronize Inputs
will not result in mixed outputs.

A combination of tunnels and funnels can be used to create item streams with a particular ratio of item types. For example, forming brass ingots in a mixer requires an equal number of copper ingots and zinc ingots. This equal mix can be provided by feeding the copper and zinc ingots from individual chests through brass funnels set to the same stack size. The ingots are then fed by belt to two tunnels forming a group set to
Synchronize Inputs
. All outputs but one need to be filtered to reject copper and zinc ingots. The remaining output will have a properly balanced blend to feed into the mixer.

The brass workshop, unsurprisingly, allows you to create
Brass Ingots
which opens up quite a lot of capabilities such as automated planting, item sorting, advanced redstone circuits, ore processors, and elevators. It requires access to the Nether to obtain a
Blaze
.

sections.Components:
The brass workshop builds off the
Starter Workshop
but adds a
Blaze Burner
for the
heated mixing
required to make brass. It also adds a belt mechanism to automate bulk processing of brass. The brass workshop requires no more rotational power than the starter workshop, so the power system remains the same with the exception of also driving the belt mechanism.

The brass workshop has the following components:

Crafting Table
Furnace
Stonecutter
Mechanical Press
with
Depot
Mechanical Mixer
with
Basin
Blaze Burner
Hopper
Andesite Funnel
Chest
x 5

Powering the mechanical press, mixer, and belt mechanism requires:

2x
Water Wheel
4x
Cogwheel
3x
Large Cogwheel
2x
Gearbox
4x
Shaft
2x
Mechanical Belt

Brass Workshop (front)
sections.Layout: The image "Brass Workshop (front)" shows an efficient layout. As with the starter workshop, it contains a mechanical mixer and a mechanical press. It adds a hopper to feed in recipe components, a belt feed to transport the mixer outputs and an andesite funnel to store the outputs in a chest.  The rectangular hole in the grass is there to show the belt mechanism. It can be filled in, except a space must be left open in front of the blaze burner to feed it fuel.
sections.Power Source:
Brass Workshop (back)

The power source is described in detail in the
Starter Workshop
tutorial. This design adds only a few components to drive the belt that carries the brass ingots from the mixer basin to the chest. The image "Brass Workshop (back)" shows an extra shaft extending from the third large cogwheel. This shaft drives the vertical belt down to the gearbox which in turn drives the belt carrying the brass ingots.
sections.Making Brass:
Making brass is very simple with this workshop. Simply load two stacks of
Copper Ingots
and two stacks of
Zinc Ingots
to the hopper and feed a piece of
Coal
or other fuel to the blaze burner. To automate larger production batches, add a chest on top of the hopper. This should produce about 25 brass ingots per minute and deposit them in the receiving chest.

Note that you can still produce any other mixer recipe with this setup. This design is also great for bulk production of
Andesite Alloy
.
sections.Capabilities: Brass production opens up several new lines of capabilities in Create.
sections.Automated Planting:
Create
Brass Hands
then
Deployers
to add automatic replanting to your crop and tree harvesting contraptions.
sections.Item Sorting:
Brass allows you to build
Brass Tunnels
,
Brass Funnels
, and
Smart Chutes
which, combined with mechanical belts and storage blocks, give great flexibility in sorting and routing items for production automation or sorted storage.
sections.Advanced Redstone Circuits:
Flatten brass ingots to make
Pulse Timers
,
Pulse Extenders
, and
Pulse Repeaters
. Among many other uses, these components can automatically trigger your crop and tree harvesting contraptions for unattended operation.
sections.Ore Processing:
Bulk ore processing requires
Crushing Wheels
which require brass to create. Apply brass ingots to
Stripped Logs
to create
Brass Casings
. Combine the brass casings with an
Electron Tube
and a Crafting table to create
Mechanical Crafters
. Then use the mechanical crafters to build the crushing wheels.
sections.Elevators:
Combine brass casings with
Dried Kelp Blocks
and
Iron Sheets
to make
Elevator Pulleys
.

Cardboard Packages
are part of the
High Logistics
system in Create. They are used to insert or extract items in bulk into or from storage blocks. They can also transport items in bulk between storage and a variety of tools in an automated factory.

sections.Obtaining:
Cardboard ackages are created by a
Packager
when the packager extracts items from a storage block. There are several facades for packages, all functionally the same. The facade for any particular package is selected at random. No cardboard is consumed from any inventory in creating the package.
sections.Storage:
Cardboard packages can serve as temporary storage. They have 9 slots of inventory.

Cardboard packages can be placed in any type of storage block such as a chest while remaining a package. If a packager is used to insert a package into storage, the package will be unpacked, and individual items will be stored.

When a storage block such as a
Toolbox
,
Shulker Box
, or
Minecart Contraption
is packaged, the cardboard package will only store one stack at a time.
sections.Interaction:
Cardboard packages can be placed in the world as entities either by right-clicking, dropping, or throwing them. Hold right-click to launch the package. The longer right-click is held, the greater the distance it is thrown. Right click to pick them up again.

Left click to unpack them and drop their contents. A package is instantly unpacked when it comes in contact with
Water
,
Mechanical Saws
,
Lava
, or
Cactus
. They can also be unpacked by shift-right-clicking while they are in the player inventory. Any of these methods destroys the cardboard package.
sections.Automated Routing:
On creation, cardboard packages can be given an address to be delivered to. Packages are labeled with an address when the packager receives an addressed request through a logistics network, or when a packager with an attached
Sign
is given a redstone signal.

Packages do not automatically seek out an address. Rather, packages can be sorted and rerouted while being transported by mechanical belts, chain conveyors or trains. Using a
Package Filter
on standard sorting tools in Create such as funnels and tunnels can sort packages transported on mechanical belts.
Package Frogports
can sort those on chain conveyors. And
Postboxes
can sort those being transported by train. Other than the postbox, the final destination of a package is not given an address label.

The following blocks can be used to request deliveries to an address:

Redstone Requester
Stock Ticker
Factory Gauge

Create uses a
glob
(also known as a
wildcard
) to specify addresses for sorting. Globs are not as powerful as
RegEx
(regular expressions), but they are easier to learn.

sections.Usage:
The Cart Assembler can be placed on
Rails
. When the assembler is powered with redstone, blocks placed on top of the assembler will be attached to minecarts that pass through it as a
Contraption
. Use
Block Attachment Utilities
to attach more blocks.
sections.Value Settings:
The
Value Settings Screen
can be accessed on the side of the Cart Assembler to change the cart contraption's movement modes.

Always face toward motion
Pause actors while rotating -
Contraption Actors
such as a
Deployer
will not work while the cart rotates.
Lock Rotation - the contraption will not change alignment along with the cart, and will retain the same rotation from when it was built, much like the effect of a
Mechanical Bearing
on a cart contraption.
sections.Cart Contraptions:
Similarly to rotating structures, having a
Mechanical Bearing
in the structure will cause the attached part to keep the same alignment as the cart moves.

Cart Contraptions made with a
Furnace Minecart
can automatically take
Coal
as fuel from onboard inventories.

Despite having collision with mobs or items, Cart Contraptions do not collide with blocks unless the appropriate world-interaction block makes the collision.

Cart contraptions will
not
travel through nether portals.

Cart Contraptions can be taken into the inventory by right clicking them with a
Wrench
(
Configurable
.) Excluding entities, this keeps all storage and cart configuration. By default, if certain blocks are present on the Cart Contraption, such as
Spawners
or
Budding Amethyst
, the contraption cannot be picked up with a
Wrench
(
Configurable
.) By default, Cart Contraption items cannot be placed in inventories such as
Shulker Boxes
or
Toolboxes
(
Configurable
.)
sections.Carriage Contraptions:
Carriage contraptions are moving structures connected directly to two minecarts.

Carriage Contraptions can be made by connecting two Cart Assemblers with minecarts using a structure. This will not work if the two minecarts are linked together by
Minecart Coupling
.

Carriage contraptions can also be disassembled by right clicking with a
Wrench
.

Aside from movement, there is no difference between the functions of a Carriage Contraption and a Single Cart Contraption. However, the smoother movement is better for moving mobs or items with only collision.
sections.History:
Added the Cart Assembler (Very important. It led to so many updates and players innovating.)
Fixed Minecart contraptions killing their own mount using
Mechanical Saws
/
Drills
.
Fixed Cart Assemblers blocking in the powered rail kickstart logic.

Cart Assemblers can now be configured to 3 different rotation modes.
Minecarts with mounted contraptions can now be picked up as an item.
Furnace Minecarts can now be used in the Cart Assembler.
Fixed displaced coordinates between contraptions and their mounts to fix minecart contraptions disappearing when loaded near chunk borders.

Changed the way Cart Assemblers react to redstone input.
Fixed crash when assembled minecarts pick up the block below their assembler.

Fixed server crash when Cart Assembler accelerates held Minecarts.

Cart Assemblers now have several behaviours depending on the rail type they were placed on.

Contraptions can now be mounted between two Minecarts.
Chest Minecarts can now be used in the Cart Assembler.
Minecarts can no longer be moved while a contraption is stalling them.
Moved option input of cart assemblers to side faces.
Fixed activator rails not diassembling furnace minecart contraptions.
Fixed drills continuing to dig at old locations when placing a minecart structure somewhere else.
Cart contraptions now keep their item name.

Cart Assemblers can now be placed on controller rails.

Minecarts can now collide with non-mounted contraptions.

Fixed minecart contraptions started on a powered rail facing in unwanted directions.
Fixed powered rail Cart Assemblers not respecting the solid block rule of powered rails.
Fixed minecart contraption items not facing away from the player when placed.
Fixed duplication of Cart Assemblers.

Minecart Contraptions with exceeding NBT packet sizes can no longer be picked up.

Cart Assemblers now have a specific direction.
Assembled cart contraptions assemble and disassemble according to the assembler's direction.
Cart contraptions no longer turn exponentially.
Cart contraption now turn more sluggishly the larger they are.
Some changes to the Cart Assembler model.
Fixed wrenching of cart contraptions being able to duplicate items.
Cart contraptions with attached

sections.Catches fire from lava:
Casings
are blocks used throughout many crafting recipes in Create, as well as for decoration and aesthetic purposes.

There are four types of Casings:
Andesite
Casings are mainly used in basic contraptions,
Brass
Casings are used in more advanced machines,
Copper
Casings are strictly for fluids, and
Train
Casings for locomotive transportation.

sections.Manual Item Application:
Casings can only be crafted through physically applying a valid alloy or ingot to any Stripped variant of Log or Wood. The logs will convert themselves into the casing, where the player can either mine it with their preferred tool or use a
Wrench
to place the casing in their inventory.
sections.Encasing:
Copper Casings can be used to prevent Pipes from connecting to each other. Note the casing over the three-way connection in the bottom image has isolated the top tank.

Mechanical Belts
,
Shafts
, and
Cogwheels
can be encased in most casings, creating a decoration around the encased block. Copper casings, however, can be used only on
Fluid Pipes
. Likewise, a fluid pipe will not accept any other kind of casing.

Although mostly decorative, casings can also be used to control multiple connections. Applying a casing to a pipe will prevent it from connecting to any additional pipes placed after the casing was applied, save for directly in front of the pipe opening. Casings on
Cogwheels
can prevent cogs from connecting to other cogs via the shaft. This allows cogs to be placed right next to each other without affecting each other. A
Wrench
applied to the face of the casing will toggle the shaft connection on and off.

sections.Placement:
After placing a Chain Conveyor, they can be connected to other Chain Conveyors by right-clicking them with a
Chain
. The selection can be cleared by right-clicking the Chain Conveyor again. The Chain Conveyor requires 1 chain for every
2
2
3
{\displaystyle 2{\frac {2}{3}}}
blocks between the two Chain Conveyors.

The maximum distance at which chain conveyors can be placed is 32 blocks, can add 8 blocks to the side if it is 32 blocks away (End and start is counted), and can be modified in config.

Maximum slope and placement distance of a Chain Conveyor

The maximum angle at which chain conveyors can connect with elevation difference is 45°, plus an additional 2 blocks horizontal distance. The maximum distance at 45° slope is 23 blocks horizontal by 21 blocks vertical (center to center).
sections.Stress Network:
Chain Conveyors can be used to transfer
Kinetic Stress
. As with normal Stress Network rules, the Stress Capacity of the network is added together and the rotation speed is taken to be the speed of the fastest-rotating unit. Also like other Stress-transferring components, the Chain Conveyor and/or the Chain connection breaks when a part of the network tries to contribute a rotational force in the opposite direction. The broken Conveyor and/or Chains drop as items.

Stress transfer does not require the intermediate chunks to be loaded. However, chain or conveyor breakage may happen over a long-distance network of Chain Conveyors due to chunk-loading ideosyncracies.
sections.Transport:
Right-click a Chain Conveyor with a
Wrench
to take a ride. Sneak to dismount. If the player right-clicks a chain while riding, the player is teleported to the target chain at the position of the right-click.

This can be the same chain or a different chain.

If the player collides with a block while riding, they will be thrown off.

When passing a Chain Conveyor, the player will be sent in the direction they’re looking towards. This can be an intersection or just a U-turn.

Cardboard Packages
can be placed on Chain Conveyors via right-click.
Package Frogports
are used to automatically move
Cardboard Packages
from and to the Chain Conveyors. Chain Conveyors will automatically sort packages by their
Address
to send them to Frogports with a matching
Address
.

The Chain Conveyor has a transmission ratio of

sections.Transferring Items:
Chutes can extract items from inventories or belts immediately above them and insert or deposit items on inventories or belts below them. Chutes will also collect items that fall upon them and will drop items into empty space if an inventory is not immediately below them. Chutes may be stacked either pure vertically or in a vertical diagonal to form a pipe for moving items.

If the receiving inventory is full, chutes will hold one stack internally and stop accepting more items. Chutes cannot insert or extract items from the sides of inventories, although funnels may be used to insert or extract items from the sides of chutes. Chutes are limited to no more than 16 items in a stack while Smart Chutes can transport up to 64 items in a stack.

Since Create 6.0.7, Chutes can also insert compostable items into a
Composter
from the top, like a faster and cheaper version of the vanilla
Hopper
.
[
1
]
Because of how the Composter works, the Chute always inserts one item at a time. It does this by taking from the source (above) inventory a whole stack size, storing it inside the chute's internal stack, and transferring items down one-by-one in the internal stack. A Chute placed below can also extract the
Bone Meal
from the Composter.
sections.Encased FanPowered Chutes:
Items in chutes will be affected by gravity and tumble downward by default. To push or pull items up, a powered
Encased Fan
is needed under or on top of the chutes respectively. For instance, a fan below the chutes would push items up and a fan above the chutes would pull items up. The
speed
of the
Encased Fan
can change how fast items go upwards.
sections.Splitting & Merging: Multiple lines of chutes can merge into one, though the items will not merge into one stack. Without Smart Chutes, Fan powered chutes will initially prefer certain paths before overflowing into other lines if possible. Pushing Fan powered Chutes that split into multiple lines will prefer the straightest path. Pulling Fan powered chutes will draw the items to the powered fan. The airflow and the resulting item speed can increase or decrease as the Chutes merge and split, respectively.
sections.Appearance:
From left to right, a Chute, an encased Chute, and a
Block of Industrial Iron
.

Chutes can be right clicked with a
Wrench
to be given windows.  Right clicking again removes the windows. Non-diagonal chutes can also be encased with
Industrial Iron Blocks
simply by clicking on the chute with an industrial iron block. The blocks are not consumed. To remove the industrial iron block appearance, simply click the chute with a wrench. Diagonal chutes already appear the same as encased Chutes.
sections.Smart Chutes:
Smart Chutes behave similarly to
Brass Funnels
. They can be
filtered
to only allow certain items through, configured to pass specific stack sizes (up to 64), and stopped with a redstone signal. Unlike funnels, they can insert and extract at the same time, but can only function vertically.

To restrict the Smart Chute to passing a single type of item, simply click the filter slot with the item. Clicking with a different item will change the filter to the new item. To remove a filter, click with an empty hand. Smart Chutes can also be configured to filter multiple item types by using a List or Attribute
Filter
.

When directly below an inventory, the filter slot doubles as a
Value Settings
control, much like the
Brass Funnel
. The Chute can be adjusted to extract up to or exactly a set amount of items per stack. The
Value Settings
of a Smart Chute will be saved even when the inventory above is destroyed,

sections.Intro:
Create adds several components that can be used in redstone circuits. These include the
Redstone Contact
,
Redstone Link
,
Linked Controller
,
Pulse Repeater
,
Pulse Extender
,
Pulse Timer
,
Powered Latch
, and
Powered Toggle Latch
.  These components can make redstone circuits simpler and smaller as well as giving finer control over timing.

sections.Logic Gates: Logic gates are circuits that provide a digital output signal based on the conditions of one or more input signals. Digital signals are either on or off (powered or unpowered redstone) and usually represented as a 1 or 0 respectively.
sections.NOT GATE:
The ability to place the
Pulse Extender
in an inverse output mode allows it to be used as a NOT gate. Simply set the pulse length to 2 ticks (or as needed for your particular circuit) and right click the Pulse Extender to toggle to inverse mode.

A Powered Latch can also be used for a NOT gate. A continuously powered signal is sent to the set input and the control signal is sent to the reset input.
sections.AND, OR, NAND, and NOR Gates:
A simple pattern of three
Pulse Extenders
can act as an AND, OR, NAND, or NOR gate depending only on the selection of inverse settings among the Pulse Extenders. If we label the two input Pulse Extenders A and B, and the output O, then the following table shows the Normal (N) versus Inverse (
I
) setting of each Pulse Extender to achieve the indicated gate. (Note that there are smaller circuit options for some of the gates.)
sections.XOR Gate:
Pulse Extenders
can be used to create a single layer XOR Gate. The design shown below uses repeaters to push charges into opaque blocks which act as diodes providing isolated signals to both the redstone dust continuing to the right and the redstone dust between the two blocks. The center Pulse Extender injects an inverted signal into another block which also acts as an isolating diode forming independent OR Gates with the redstone dust on the far side and near side of the block. All three of the Pulse Extenders are in the inverted mode.
sections.Pulse Timer Clock:
Pulse Timer

The
Pulse Timer
is itself a clock. It repeatedly emits a short pulse with a user-set delay between pulses. Note that the short pulse may not be long enough to have the desired effect (such as starting a minecart with a powered rail). In this case, place a Redstone Repeater or a Pulse extender between the pulse timer and the item to be powered.

Clicking on the pulse timer inverts the output signal. Applying a redstone signal to the side of the pulse timer with the small triangle will inhibit the pulse.
sections.Pulse Repeater Clock: A Pulse Repeater along with a Redstone Repeater can make a pulse clock where a short pulse is repeatedly sent out with a selectable delay between pulses.  In the clock shown below, the Redstone Repeater must have at least 1 tick delay. A pulse input on any of the redstone lines will start the clock. Note that the pulse from a button is too long and will interfere with the feedback signal from the repeater. To start the clock, you can quickly switch a lever on and off or you can feed a button output through another Pulse Repeater set to 2 ticks. The delay between pulses is controlled by the delay setting on the Pulse Repeater.
sections.Variable Cycle Clock: Two pulse extenders, one in inverse mode, can make a clock with independently settable on and off durations. The clock will start itself when one of the two pulse extenders is set to inverse mode.
sections.Signal Comparators: Signal comparators compare the strength of two input signals from which they output a signal based on the similarity or difference in the two input signals.
sections.Matching Signal-Strength Detector:
A matching signal-strength detector emits a signal when the strengths of two input signals are equal. When the input signals are unequal, the detector output is off.

The circuit shown below will detect matching signal strengths between 1 and 15. In this circuit, the comparator on the right is in subtraction mode, causing it to subtract the strength of the signal entering the side from the strength of the signal entering the base. The circuit will trigger an output signal when the output of the comparator on the right is of strength one. This means the left side signal must be reduced by one, which is done here by the string of two redstone dust.

The output of the subtraction comparator is fed to a pulse extender acting as an inverter and a repeater acting as a one-way diode. The output of these two devices is ORed then input to another pulse extender acting as an inverter. The circuit output will be ON only when the outputs of both the pulse extender and the repeater are off. This condition will occur only when the output power of the subtraction comparator is exactly one, powering the pulse extender inverter but not the repeater.

If the strength of the side signal is
greater
than the base signal, the subtraction will be negative. The comparator will put out no signal. The pulse extender inverter will therefore output a signal which then turns off the circuit's final output.  If the strength of the side signal is
less
than the base signal, then the subtraction comparator will put out a signal strength of at least two, thus ensuring that both the pulse extender inverter and the repeater are powered. In this case, the signal from the repeater turns off the circuit's final output.

This simple circuit will not detect matching strengths of zero. Also, if the left signal is zero and the right signal is one, the circuit will give a false positive result. Care must be taken that the left side signal never be less than one.

One use for a matching strength detector is to create a combination lock. Only when a player sets the proper signal strength will a desired action occur. Multiple circuits can be ORed together prior to the final inverter to create a multi-digit combination lock.

sections.Usage:
A Clipboard with a
Schematicannon
Checklist.

Use
a clipboard in hand or
use
a placed clipboard to access its interface. Items on the checklist can be written out or checked off, or all checked items can be erased.
sections.Placement:
Sneak
use
a clipboard to place it on the ground.
Sneak
use
it again or break it to pick it up.
sections.Copying and Pasting:
Use
the clipboard on a block with
Value Settings
to copy them, such as a
Brass Funnel
or a
Mechanical Bearing
, then left click another to paste them. When pasting a setting including a filter, having a filter in the inventory will be required to paste the setting.

Clicking a placed Clipboard with an item Clipboard will add the placed Clipboard's entries onto the item Clipboard's entries. This will not allow duplicate entries.
sections.Schematicannon:
Put the Clipboard in a ready
Schematicannon
to get the Schematicannon's Checklist. Like with a
Book and Quill
, the Clipboard's checklist can be updated by putting it in the Schematicannon again. Items can also be checked off manually. Once finished with the Schematicannon's checklist, the Clipboard can be blanked again by either using the "Erase checked items" option, or putting it through the
Crafting Grid
When holding a Clipboard containing a Schematicannon checklist (or any item checklist),
Right-Clicking
on a Shopkeeper with the clipboard will automatically add all the missing/required items from the checklist directly into the order menu. This allows players to quickly order all necessary building materials in bulk without having to manually select each item.
sections.Displaying Text:
A clipboard can also paste text written in it to a
Display Board
or
Nixie Tubes
. Nixie Tubes will only take text from the Clipboard's first bullet point, whereas Display Boards will attempt to display all of a Clipboard's points from the Clipboard's selected page. Pasting text onto a
Display Board
from a Clipboard works much like using a
Name Tag
on it.
sections.Addresses:
Addresses
can be saved to the Clipboard by right-clicking a
Package Frogport
or
Postbox
. They can also be added manually by typing the desired address with a # at the beginning.

This allows the clipboard to suggest and autofill Addresses in relevant GUIs when in the player's inventory or placed within 32 blocks of the player.

Clicking the addresses in the clipboard's GUI disables them and prevents them from showing up as a suggestion. They can be re enabled by clicking them again. Disabled addresses count as "checked," and will be deleted when erasing checked items.

sections.Usage:
When
Powered
by kinetics:

Starts rotating the attached structure towards the current hour. If an independent second structure exists in front of the first one, it will serve as the minute hand.

The
Value Settings Screen
can be accessed from the side of the block, and can be used to change the order of the hands or switch to a 24-hour reading resembling the
Clock
item.

Like the normal
Clock
, the Clockwork Bearing cannot tell the time in the
Nether
. Instead, it constantly rotates.

A clock made with a Clockwork Bearing and Nixie Tubes.

Cogwheels have three main methods of interlocking:

Two Cogwheels interlock when placed next to each other (not diagonally) and facing the same direction. When rotational force is provided to one of the cogwheels, the force will be provided to the other Cogwheel at the same speed but in the opposite direction.
Two
Large Cogwheels
interlock when placed perpendicular to each other, effectively changing its axis and direction, but not its speed.
A Cogwheel and a Large Cogwheel interlock when placed diagonally to each other and facing the same direction. The Large Cogwheel will rotate at half the speed of the Cogwheel.

A cogwheel can also be used like a
Shaft
, conveying rotation from the ends of its axis. They can be stopped from doing this by applying a
Casing
, configurable with a
Wrench
. Mechanical components can be connected to each end, and several Cogwheels connected end-to-end function the same as multiple shafts would.
sections.RPM Enhancing Rigs:
Using pairs of Cogwheels and Large Cogwheels, rotational speed can be easily doubled or halved using the mechanic mentioned above. It is possible to connect many pairs of Large Cogwheels and Cogwheels to apply this mechanic repeatedly, up to 256 RPM (Though that limit can be increased or decreased in the
Config
).

A Large Cogwheel can also be connected to a
Rotation Speed Controller
, to adjust speed more precisely.
sections.Activating Components:
Some blocks need to be powered by a Cogwheel to function. Those blocks contain a Cogwheel in their texture and can be powered by placing a Cogwheel adjacent to them or a large Cogwheel diagonally, both in the same direction as the block, like a normal Cogwheel.

Components that can only be powered by cogwheels :

Display Board
Mechanical Arm
Mechanical Crafter
Mechanical Mixer
Millstone
does not have a
Shaft
on the bottom side)
Mechanical Pump

Conductors are special passive mobs in Create:Steam 'n' rails.

They can be constructed by placing any conductor hat on an andesite casing; they can also be made using deployers.

Conductor wearing a red conductor cap

Conductor will wear the conductor cap you used to make them.

Uses of the Conductor

Conductors can be used to transport toolboxes by right clicking them but they cannot walk by themselves so you need to right click them with lead to make them follow you around if you wish to remove the toolbox sneak click the conductor.

Conductors can pull levers and push buttons by looking at them, if you put buttons and levers all around they can only press one button/lever randomly. If you are wearing a hat that is different from the conductor's hat the conductor is currently wearing they will not respond.

Upon right-click, a conductor can be given
Engineer's Goggles
. Then, you can bind a remote lens to that conductor by right-clicking it with the lens. Bound conductors can share their point of view in a camera-like screen when the bound remote lens is right-clicked in the air. It is also possible to move around as the conductor in this mode. Press shift to exit.

Conductor Whistle

The conductor whistle can be used to call the train anywhere on the track. Right click a seated conductor acting as a train controller with a conductor whistle to bind the whistle to that train. Right clicking the track will call the train to that spot on the track. Right clicking a station with the whistle will call the train to the station.

Conductor whistles work with deployers on train stations and also with tracks (with exceptions). A deployer used on a train station with the whistle will work as normal. A deployer used on a track with a whistle will automatically call the train in the positive direction of that coordinate. This means that trains can only be called to move in the +x or +z directions with deployers on tracks.

Redstone Controlled Conductors/Trains

Right clicking the conductor with a redstone link will make the conductor redstone controllable and is indicated by a redstone receiver being added to its hat. To control the conductor, set the frequencies you want for the conductor on a linked controller and right click the conductor with the linked controller (there is no indicator for this). You should now be able to use the linked controller to move the conductor around.

The frequencies set in the linked controller that you right clicked the conductor with will be stored in the conductor. For example: if you set the frequency for "forward" using stone in red and wood in blue on your linked controller and right clicked the conductor with it, you can now make the conductor move forward by placing down a redstone link with stone in red and wood in blue and powering it.

If the conductor is seated and controlling a train, you can use redstone links or linked controllers to drive the train remotely. Holding "shift" or "space" will make the train move and stop at the next station. If the train isn't moving, holding "shift" or "space" and pressing in the direction you want to go will make the train go to the station in that direction.

As of the latest update, the conductor cannot reverse trains through redstone control, even if it has access to both train controls. It can still travel to stations in the reverse direction by holding "shift" or "space" and pressing reverse but freely controlling it in reverse is not possible at the moment.

Conductor Caps
are a craftable item added with Create: Steam 'n rails.

They can be coloured with any dye.

The player can wear a cap or decide to turn it into a

sections.Secret caps:
There are secret names for caps that change their appearance.

Adding [sus] before the name (no space between) will make the player wearing the cap look like a conductor.

IThundxr's [sus] cap changes the player into IThundxr's skin

sections.Creation:
Contraptions are created when a
Movement Anchor
is activated and the attached blocks are assembled into a Contraption. Most Movement Anchors will activate when given
Rotational Force
and disassemble back into blocks when not receiving power or when the Contraption is unable to move. Others are activated manually or by
Redstone
. Most anchors have
Movement Modes
that change the conditions for when they disassemble.

A
Mechanical Bearing
on a
Mechanical Bearing
Contraption.

A minecart contraption with a
Mechanical Bearing
.

Each Movement Anchor has at least one sticky side and can move at least one block with no extra utilities. Multiple blocks can be moved with the use of
Block Attachment Utilities
such as:

Linear Chassis
Radial Chassis
Super Glue
Sticker
Slime Block
Honey Block

Blocks that attach to other blocks, such as
Lever
s,
Sign
s, or
Torch
es, will automatically become part of the Contraption. Blocks that automatically attach to other blocks of the same type, such as
Sails
,
Piston Extension Poles
,
Mechanical Belts
, and
Gantry Shafts
, only need to be glued in one place.

Blocks can stick to sticky chassis, but chassis won't stick to blocks on their own. Slime Blocks on Contraptions will not pick up Honey Blocks and vice versa, and neither will pick up
Glazed Terracotta
. They will still pick up other blocks such as
Furnace
s.

A
Mechanical Bearing
can be added to a Contraption to attach a second Contraption that keeps one alignment as the structure moves. It can be attached at any orientation.

Certain blocks cannot be moved by Contraptions by default. Other blocks can be moved, but when on
Minecart Contraptions
, the cart cannot be picked up with a
Wrench
. For certain blocks, this is adjustable in the
config
. Movement Anchors are also unmovable while they are active.

Most Movement Anchors have movement modes that can be changed through their
Value Settings Screen
by hovering over their side and holding right-click to access the interface. Most anchors include "Always place when stopped," "Only place near starting position," and "Only place when anchor is destroyed," determining when the blocks are placed back into the world.
Cart Assemblers
have "always face movement," "pause actors while rotating," and "lock rotation."
sections.Collision:
Gantry Carriages
,
Rope Pulleys
, and
Mechanical Pistons
will stop moving if an unmovable block or set of blocks is in their path.
Trains
,
Cart Assembler
Contraptions,
Elevator Pulleys
, and
Bearings
will only collide with blocks if the appropriate world interaction block makes the collision.

Entities will also collide with Contraptions.
sections.Contraption Actors:
Blocks that have special functions on Contraptions.

Rings each time the contraption's momentum changes.
Haunted Bells
will highlight areas where mobs can spawn when this happens.
Placed in the center of a Bearing contraption, it will toll for every full rotation.
In the center of a Minecart Contraption, it will toll every time the Cart starts or stops. To the left or right, it tolls for every left or right turn, respectively.
On
Trains
, the bell will ring shortly before the train arrives at a station after traveling a distance.
